title: Instagram post (feed image, carousel or Reel, with caption)

gates.text: Truth: no claim, number, customer, quote, result or 'bestseller' label that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research, on slides, in the script or in the caption. Missing facts are visible [NEEDS FACT: ...] questions.

Limits and format: 5 hashtags or fewer; caption under 2,200 characters with the hook in the first ~125; carousel 20 slides or fewer; Reel 3 minutes or shorter; every image or slide has alt text; every Reel has burned-in captions and text kept out of the bottom ~20% and right edge.

Policy and originality: no engagement bait (tag a friend, comment YES, like if), no reposted or watermarked content, no unlicensed music, no fake screenshots or reviews, no stock people presented as customers or staff, no banned phrases from copy-fundamentals.

anchors.1: Logo, title card, greeting or a static product shot with no hook.
anchors.3: Clear hook and image, but the payoff is held back or the headline runs long.
anchors.5: Payoff-first visual with a specific hook (10 words or fewer on slide 1, 8 or fewer on a Reel's first frame) that works on its own in the feed.

anchors.1: Pure promotion; nobody would save or send it.
anchors.3: Mildly useful or pleasant, but no obvious person to send it to.
anchors.5: A reader would send it to a specific person or save it to use later; the send or save reason is built into the content.

anchors.1: Repetitive or random order; several points per slide or beat.
anchors.3: Logical order, one point each, but slides don't create a reason to keep swiping or watching.
anchors.5: Each slide or beat carries one point and opens a loop the next one closes; summary slide and single CTA land the idea.

anchors.1: Vague adjectives (handmade with love, amazing quality); no numbers or process.
anchors.3: Some real details, but the central claim lacks a number, mechanism or quote.
anchors.5: Central claim carried by a confirmed number, process detail or permitted customer phrase; unmistakably this business.

anchors.1: Emoji wall or hashtag block; first line wasted; generic tags.
anchors.3: Readable caption with sensible tags, but the first line doesn't stand alone or lacks the search phrase.
anchors.5: First ~125 characters stand alone with the search phrase; caption adds what the visual lacks; 3-5 specific CamelCase tags.

anchors.1: No visual direction, or needs a studio, crew, models or stock.
anchors.3: Visuals described but vague ("nice product photo") or some shots impractical for a small business.
anchors.5: Slide-by-slide or shot-by-shot brief the owner can produce with a phone and existing assets in one session, using real photos or footage.

anchors.1: No alt text, no captions, text on low-contrast or busy backgrounds.
anchors.3: Alt text present but generic ("product photo"); captions mentioned but not specified.
anchors.5: Alt text per image describing subject, action and on-image text; burned-in captions; readable contrast; CamelCase hashtags.

anchors.1: Generic brand voice or hype; off-positioning.
anchors.3: Clean and on-brand but not tied to a specific pillar, objection or customer phrase.
anchors.5: Sounds like the owner; expresses one positioning element in the customer's words.

anchors.3: Clear ask but generic, or more than one ask.
anchors.5: One ask matched to awareness (save, send to a named kind of person, or link in bio with exactly what they'll find).
